title: HelixDTA: Dual-Branch Sequence-Structure Learning with Complete Target Structures for Robust and Interpretable Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
authors: Lou, Shang; Li, Xuhua; Peng, Yujie; Yuan, Yuan; Peng, Bo; Yi, Yingyu; Zhang, Xuchao; Zhao, Hailong; Wang, Beilei; Li, Kun; Qian, Hong; Ren, Tao; Gu, Hongcang; Zhang, Fan
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 提出双分支深度学习框架HelixDTA，融合蛋白序列与完整结构预测药物-靶标亲和力，虽以药物靶点为核心但涉及蛋白结构建模，方法可迁移至蛋白质结构相关计算。
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target affinity (DTA) is crucial for accelerating the discovery of drug candidates. Despite recent advances in machine learning methods, existing models often rely solely on either sequence information or protein pocket structures. This limitation prevents these models from fully capturing the critical three-dimensional (3D) physical information that governs molecular recognition, thus failing to meet the high-precision demands of drug discovery. To address this, we introduce HelixDTA, a deep learning framework featuring a parallel dual-branch architecture that independently learns representations from two distinct but complementary modalities: sequence context and complete target structures. By integrating sequence-derived features with structure-derived features at the prediction layer, this architecture preserves modality-specific insights while characterizing drug-target interactions more comprehensively. HelixDTA achieved strong and competitive performance on the Davis and KIBA benchmarks and maintained clear advantages across most similarity-based cold-start settings, demonstrating robust generalization to compounds with unseen scaffolds and novel protein targets. Furthermore, its built-in attention mechanism enhances interpretability by highlighting molecular regions that contribute to affinity prediction. Finally, a WRN case study demonstrates the potential use of HelixDTA for structure-aware allosteric candidate prioritization by integrating complete target-level structural context with docking-based pose inspection. In conclusion, HelixDTA offers a highly accurate, interpretable, and robust solution for DTA prediction. It highlights the value of integrating structural context with sequence-derived information and demonstrates significant potential to empower precision drug design and accelerate the drug discovery pipeline.
abstract_zh: 药物-靶点亲和力（drug-target affinity, DTA）的准确预测对于加速候选药物发现至关重要。尽管机器学习方法近期取得了进展，现有模型往往仅依赖序列信息或蛋白质口袋结构。这一局限性阻碍了这些模型充分捕捉控制分子识别的关键三维（3D）物理信息，从而无法满足药物发现的高精度需求。为解决此问题，我们引入了HelixDTA，一种深度学习框架，采用并行双分支架构，独立地从两种不同但互补的模态中学习表征：序列上下文和完整靶点结构。通过在预测层整合序列衍生特征与结构衍生特征，该架构保留了模态特定见解，同时更全面地刻画药物-靶点相互作用。HelixDTA在Davis和KIBA基准上取得了强劲且具有竞争力的性能，并在大多数基于相似性的冷启动设置中保持明显优势，展示了对具有未见骨架化合物和新颖蛋白质靶点的稳健泛化能力。此外，其内置注意力机制通过突出贡献于亲和力预测的分子区域，增强了可解释性。最后，一项WRN案例研究展示了HelixDTA在结构感知变构候选物优先排序中的潜在应用，通过整合完整靶点级结构上下文与基于对接的构象检查。总之，HelixDTA为DTA预测提供了一种高精度、可解释且稳健的解决方案。它强调了将结构上下文与序列衍生信息整合的价值，并展示了赋能精准药物设计和加速药物发现流程的巨大潜力。
